source.title: The Singular Value Decompositions of Transformer Weight Matrices are Highly Interpretable

record.tranche_reason: The post discusses superposition and feature-as-direction hypotheses, but its experiments analyze and edit SVD directions of weights. They do not test whether sparse features exceed network dimensions, whether features are stored in superposition, or the dimensionality of represented features.
record.gate_note: The post cites toy-model superposition and proposes that directions may be a useful representation, but does not test the versions listed. Its own relevant results concern semantic interpretability of weight SVD directions and effects of ablating them. SVD tracing settings and prompt details used only to configure the method are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The post projects SVD directions of GPT2 weight matrices (OV, MLP in/out) into token space and rates them for interpretability. It cites toy-model superposition and features-as-directions as motivation but does not test sparse features exceeding dimensions, capacity-driven polysemanticity, SAE recovery or feature dimensionality. The 'antipodal superposition' remarks are interpretive, and the authors say the activation-space version is untested. Its own claims of features-as-directions support are argument, not a test of any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that SVD directions of OV and MLP weights in GPT2 are highly interpretable and can be used to selectively edit model behaviour, and they read this as relatively strong support for linear features-as-directions in residual networks. They add that single-direction edits rarely change global behaviour, because processing is distributed, and that the method cannot capture nonlinear representations.
record.recipe_differences: The post analyzes weight-matrix SVD directions and does not reproduce the toy-model superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Automated interpretability classifications were reported as sensitive to few-shot example number and type, prompt format, and choice of GPT3 versus Instruct-GPT3; GPT2-medium MLP output-weight interpretability peaked in middle layers, unlike its more monotonic MLP input-weight pattern.

fits_no_version.finding: SVD directions of GPT2 MLP weights were frequently classified as semantically interpretable. Fractions rose with block depth, and manual labels showed an inverted-U across singular-vector index.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Many projected SVD directions of GPT2 MLP weights align with semantically interpretable token clusters.

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating the 'fire' OV singular vector (L22H3) lowered the log-prob of 'fire' more than other ablations; ablating the antipodal 'ice' vector raised it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ablating an OV-circuit SVD direction can differentially affect logits associated with its projected semantic cluster.

fits_no_version.finding: Random Gaussian matrices showed no semantic structure under the same projection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Semantic interpretability of projected SVD directions is absent in random matrices.

record.problems: Interpretability labels were subjective; the authors report noisy automated classifications, prompt sensitivity, and no ground-truth labels. The text gives few exact numerical results, and the reported SVD-direction interpretability does not directly establish properties of activation-space features or superposition.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows were left out. Numerical values visible only in unprovided plots and notebook material were not inferred.

untested.parts: All: no toy model, no sparsity sweep, no measure of feature geometry.
All: the remark that MLPs are more polysemantic due to limited capacity is speculation, not measured.
All: weight SVD only; no activation analysis or dictionary/SAE (sparse coding mentioned only as future work in comments).
All: assumes linear 1-D directions; nonlinear or multidimensional representations are acknowledged as outside the method.

record.verdict_notes: The informal claim that most individual neurons look polysemantic comes from playing with another paper's code; it is unquantified and not a result here. Antipodal fire/ice pairs are weight-space observations; the authors state the activation-space hypothesis is untested. Comments note SVD cannot recover overcomplete (JL) packings, and that near-equal singular values make the vectors unstable.

versions.untested_parts: Whether networks store more sparse features than dimensions as overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions; sparsity-dependent transitions and regular geometry.
Whether feature competition for limited capacity causes neuron polysemanticity, or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Whether LLM activations spread features across neurons or contain sparse features recoverable by a dictionary or SAE.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units of model representation.
Whether the model's represented or superposed features are inherently one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: GPT2-medium
rows.operation_detail: Manually classified MLP input-weight SVD directions for semantic interpretability.

conditions.value: 40 singular directions per each of 24 MLP blocks

rows.measure: Fraction of directions classified as interpretable
rows.value: The fraction increases with block depth; the post describes later blocks as having approximately 70-80% of the top 50 singular vectors highly interpretable.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviation across singular directions is shown in the plot; numeric values not stated.
rows.note: The post says manual labels were subjective and that ambiguous cases were generally rejected. The stated approximately 70-80% semantic-token criterion is a classification rule, not an independently measured feature property.
rows.check: The value mixes two things. The '70-80% of top 50 singular vectors' figure is an intro summary for later blocks. The manual labelling actually covered 40 directions per block (960 total), and 70-80% is also the token-alignment threshold used to label a direction. The row should state the per-block increase with depth and not conflate the threshold with the outcome.

rows.subject: GPT2-small, GPT2-medium, and GPT2-large (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: GPT2-small, GPT2-medium, and GPT2-large; parameter counts not stated
rows.operation_detail: Used GPT3 and a verifier to classify MLP SVD directions for interpretability.
rows.measure: Fraction of directions classified as interpretable
rows.value: Approximately 70-80% of directions are interpretable across the models; the post also describes fractions rising from about 40-50% to about 80-90% across block size.
rows.note: The percentages are reported as suite-level summaries; the post says the results are noisy and gives no separate exact values for each model.

rows.subject: GPT2-small, GPT2-medium, and GPT2-large (aggregate)
rows.size_stated: GPT2-small, GPT2-medium, and GPT2-large; parameter counts not stated
rows.operation_detail: Compared automated interpretability classifications across MLP blocks.
rows.measure: Fraction of directions classified as interpretable by block
rows.value: The post reports an increase in interpretability in later blocks, with a decline in the final layers appearing in all models; GPT2-medium MLP output weights peak in the middle, while its MLP input weights climb more monotonically.
rows.note: The post describes these patterns as noisy and does not provide numerical values by block in the text.
rows.check: 'partial' has no version to be partial against. The pattern the post states (later layers more interpretable, a final-layer dip, GPT2-medium Wout peaking mid-network) is reported as observed, though noisy.

rows.subject: Random Gaussian matrices
rows.operation_detail: Applied the token-space SVD projection and inspected the resulting directions.
rows.measure: Presence of semantic structure in projected singular directions
rows.value: The post reports that no semantic structure emerged.
rows.note: This is a stated qualitative control; matrix sizes and quantitative comparisons are not given.

rows.subject: GPT2-medium
rows.operation_detail: Ablated the 'fire' singular vector from the layer 22, head 3 OV circuit.

conditions.value: strongly cues the word 'fire'; exact prompt not stated

rows.value: The log probability decreases substantially compared with ablating other vectors.
rows.note: No numeric log probabilities or effect sizes are stated.

rows.operation_detail: Ablated singular vector 3, described as the 'ice' vector, from the layer 22, head 3 OV circuit.

conditions.value: strongly cues the word 'fire'; exact prompt not stated

rows.note: The post describes this as an antipodal effect; no numeric log probabilities are stated.
